deepseekHarness.url.markdownDescription: Where your running dsh serves `/api`. The extension only attaches: start and manage dsh yourself, independently of VS Code. On startup or connection loss, it tries immediately, then retries every 10 seconds for up to `#deepseekHarness.retryDurationSeconds#`, then stays quiet until **DeepSeek Harness: Reconnect** or a settings change. Local loopback connections authenticate using the existing browser-session record in the configured dsh home. Remote servers can use **DeepSeek Harness: Connect with Launch URL**. Cookies are kept in VS Code SecretStorage.

deepseekHarness.home.markdownDescription: The home of your running dsh, used only to read local authentication. Empty uses `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh`. The extension does not start or configure the server.

deepseekHarness.retryDurationSeconds.markdownDescription: How long, in seconds, to keep retrying transient attachment failures. Retries wait 10 seconds between attempts and stop when this window expires; an attempt already in progress may finish afterward. Set to `0` to disable automatic retries. Afterward, use **DeepSeek Harness: Reconnect** to try again.

deepseekHarness.historyPageMessages.markdownDescription: How many messages each `session.history` call asks for. **This is not a limit on what is restored:** a reopened session is always read back to the first event of its log, however long it is — this only sets how much of it one call carries. dsh counts messages backwards from where the call starts and returns the whole contiguous range behind them, tool calls, results and token-level chunk events included, so lowering this makes each call smaller and a long session take more of them. `50` is dsh's own default.
